issues.legal_issue: Property in identified goods in a deliverable state passes under an unconditional sale even when payment or physical removal is postponed.
material_facts: The sale was of felled timber in a defined coupe, and the timber was identifiable by marks on the felled trees and their stumps.
The contract did not make delivery of the timber in later sections conditional on payment of the later instalments.
The purchaser paid the first instalment and received a boundary certificate recording that possession of the forest produce had been taken.
The surety disputed liability for the purchaser’s unpaid instalments after the unremoved timber was destroyed by fire.
issues.conclusion: The timber was specific goods in a deliverable state, and property in it passed to the purchaser when the unconditional contract was made; postponement of payment or delivery did not prevent that result.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 20 of the Sale of Goods Act, 1930, property in specific goods in a deliverable state passes when an unconditional contract for their sale is made, whether or not payment or delivery is postponed. The absence of later hammer marks did not make the felled trees unascertained because the timber was otherwise identifiable.

rule.if: surety_liability_dispute and specific_goods_identifiable and goods_in_deliverable_state and unconditional_sale_contract

predicates.surety_liability_dispute: A person who guaranteed a buyer’s payment disputes liability for the buyer’s unpaid purchase price.
predicates.specific_goods_identifiable: The goods sold are identified or ascertainable as the particular goods covered by the sale.
predicates.goods_in_deliverable_state: The goods are in a state in which the buyer is bound to take delivery under the sale.
predicates.unconditional_sale_contract: The parties have made a sale contract that does not make the transfer of ownership conditional on a further event.

issues.definition: When a surety disputes the buyer’s unpaid price and the sale is unconditional for identifiable goods ready for delivery, ownership passes to the buyer when the contract is made.

issues.legal_issue: A seller’s power to stop removal of goods to secure unpaid amounts does not, without a contractual reservation of disposal, prevent ownership from passing under an unconditional sale.
material_facts: The contract permitted payment by instalments and treated that arrangement as payment in full at the time of delivery.
The rules allowed a forest officer to stop further removal when the value of goods already removed exceeded the instalments paid.
The Forest Act treated money payable for forest produce as a charge on that produce and permitted a forest officer to take possession until payment.
Neither the contract nor the rules reserved the State’s right of disposal over the sold timber.
issues.conclusion: The power to stop removal was a statutory measure to secure payment, not a reservation of the right of disposal; it did not prevent property in the timber from passing.
issues.legal_principle: Section 25(1) of the Sale of Goods Act, 1930 applies where the seller reserves the right of disposal. Rule 8 of the Forest Contract Rules did not create such a reservation: it implemented the charge and possessory remedy in section 83 of the Forest Act, 1927. The rules treated permitted instalment payments as payment in full at delivery, so section 20 of the Sale of Goods Act governed the passing of property.

rule.if: sale_of_forest_produce and instalments_treated_as_full_payment_at_delivery and removal_stop_secures_payment and no_contractual_reservation_of_disposal

predicates.sale_of_forest_produce: The goods sold are forest produce under a contract that permits instalment payments.
predicates.instalments_treated_as_full_payment_at_d: The applicable sale arrangement treats payment by instalments as payment in full at the time of delivery.
predicates.removal_stop_secures_payment: A seller or public officer may stop removal of goods to secure payment of amounts due.
predicates.no_contractual_reservation_of_disposal: The contract does not reserve to the seller a right to retain ownership or control of disposal until a condition is fulfilled.

issues.definition: Where a forest-produce sale treats instalments as full payment at delivery, a payment-security restriction on removal does not prevent ownership from passing if the contract reserves no right of disposal.

issues.legal_issue: Formal execution of a sale contract by the competent authority after the goods are lost does not defeat a sale already made subject to that authority’s acceptance.
material_facts: At auction, the authorized officer provisionally accepted the purchaser’s bid, and the purchaser and that officer signed the contract documents on the sale date.
The competent authority signed the formal deed later, after fire had destroyed some of the timber.
The governing instructions contemplated that the competent authority might sign after the purchaser and subordinate officer, and the sale procedure allowed time for that execution.
The competent authority’s later signature completed the contract and related its execution back to the sale date.
issues.conclusion: The later signature did not invalidate the contract or prevent property from passing on the sale date, subject to acceptance by the competent authority.
issues.legal_principle: The sale was finalized on the auction date subject to acceptance by the competent authority; the later formal signature completed the deed and related back to that date. The Court applied Williams v. North China Insurance Co., L.R. (1876) 1 C.P.D. 757, in holding that, in the circumstances, ratification could take effect even after the insured loss had become known. The possibility of loss before formal execution was contemplated by the transaction and the applicable rules.

predicates.sale_contract_executed_in_stages: The sale procedure provides for the purchaser and an authorized subordinate officer to execute documents before the competent authority completes formal execution.
predicates.authorized_auction_officer_provisionally: An officer authorized to conduct the auction provisionally accepts the purchaser’s bid.
predicates.competent_authority_later_accepts_and_si: The authority empowered to approve the transaction later accepts it and signs the formal contract.
predicates.later_execution_completes_prior_sale: The later signature completes, rather than creates anew, a sale already made subject to competent approval.

issues.definition: When an authorized auction officer provisionally accepts a bid and the competent authority later signs to complete the staged sale, the later execution does not defeat the sale’s effect from the auction.
